top10.introHtml: Ranked by condition, mileage-to-year ratio, and reliability. CarGurus not available this run (geographic filter URL changed). Top picks drawn from Cars.com and AutoTrader. Updated Sep 6, 2026.

picks.whyGood: Only 34,866 miles on a V8 (M113 4.3L) cabriolet — that's exceptional for a 2001. The M113 is famously reliable, with no timing-chain roulette. Low-mileage W208 CLKs are getting harder to find; this one looks to have been garaged and lightly driven.
picks.whatToVerify: Operate the hydraulic top through 3 full open/close cycles — listen for motor strain and watch for any hesitation in the latches. Check rear-window delamination (common on 20+ year old cloth tops). Inspect rocker panels and front subframe for rust. Pull a Carfax on the title. Top-cylinder seals and coolant hoses are wear items at this age regardless of mileage.
picks.bottomLine: The rarest find in this batch — a low-mileage V8 drop-top for the price of a high-mile 4-banger.

picks.whyGood: The N54 twin-turbocharged inline-6 makes 300hp and sounds like nothing else at this price. Only 48k miles in 16+ years means this engine hasn't been stressed. The E88 1-series convertible is a true driver's car with a short wheelbase and rear-wheel drive.
picks.whatToVerify: N54 high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) — ask if ever replaced; a failing HPFP causes no-starts and is a ~$600 part. Top hydraulic pump/cylinders — cycle the top 3 times and confirm full closure. Transmission: check for any judder or hesitation at speed. Confirm charge pipe and valve cover gaskets are leak-free.
picks.bottomLine: A turbocharged BMW driver's car at half the price of a comparable Z4 — low mileage seals it.

picks.whyGood: The E64 645Ci is a 325hp naturally-aspirated V8 grand tourer with a retractable soft top. Getting one for $7,298 at 78k miles is an extraordinary deal — these routinely ask $12k+. It's a 2+2 cabin so rear passengers exist (small but present).
picks.whatToVerify: Valve stem seals — check for blue smoke on cold start; a seal job runs $2–3k. Coolant system is complex (thermostat, radiator, expansion tank) — inspect for any leak history. SMG/automatic gearbox: confirm smooth shifts. Top hydraulic operation and rear-window seam for cracks.
picks.bottomLine: A $73k luxury grand tourer at $7k — the math is absurd; just go in eyes open on maintenance.

picks.whyGood: The CLK 500 packs the 5.0L M113 V8 (302hp) into the sleek W209 body. At 82k miles and $7,900 this is strong value — the M113 routinely goes 200k+ with routine service. Private Seller Exchange listings often come from auction or consignment with dealer paperwork.
picks.whatToVerify: Fully cycle the convertible top; check for any hydraulic fluid leaks at the hose fittings under the rear quarter. Inspect front strut mounts (common wear). Ensure the Brake Assist / ABS module shows no warning lights. Rocker panels for rust.
picks.bottomLine: A V8 W209 CLK under $8k is hard to argue with — the M113 engine alone is worth the price.

picks.whyGood: CarGurus rates this a Great Deal, and the last-gen E93 3-series convertible is the sweet spot — N52 inline-6 is naturally aspirated and bulletproof compared to the turbo N54/N55. At $8,292 / 111k miles, this is a sensible fun-car purchase with predictable maintenance costs.
picks.whatToVerify: Convertible top hydraulics — full cycle test; any hesitation means a pump is going. VANOS solenoids (common $200 fix if rattling on cold start). Oil level check (N52 can consume oil). Inspect rocker panels for rust bubbles. Check for any SRS or DSC warning lights.
picks.bottomLine: Great Deal badge + last-gen naturally aspirated 3-series convertible = the safe reliable choice in this batch.

picks.whyGood: The 200 S Convertible is underrated — 283hp Pentastar V6, comfortable 4-passenger drop-top, and 66k miles at this price is genuinely good mileage for a 2013. Good Deal rating confirms the market agrees.
picks.whatToVerify: Convertible top motor and hydraulic cylinders — Chrysler 200 tops can develop slow operation over time; do a timed open/close cycle. Check for any transmission shudder (6-speed auto can be finicky). Power fold mirrors and heated seats. Inspect cloth top for any tears or brittle rear window.
picks.bottomLine: The most practical choice — 4 true seats, modern V6, low miles, Good Deal, and easy to find parts for.

picks.whyGood: The E93 335i is the performance pick — N54 twin-turbo inline-6, 300hp, in the final-gen E90 convertible body before BMW switched to harder-edged turbos. CarVision of Trooper is close to Media, PA — easy to inspect. Under 95k miles.
picks.whatToVerify: HPFP history (the N54 Achilles heel — confirm replacement or budget $600 for it). Charge pipes for cracking. Check for any coolant or oil leaks around the valve cover. Top hydraulics — full cycle test.
picks.bottomLine: A local, low-100k turbo BMW convertible — more performance than the 328i and still reasonable on maintenance.

picks.whyGood: 38,907 original miles on a 1991 Infiniti M30 convertible is extraordinary — these rarely survive with such low mileage. The VG20ET V6 is robust. A collector-grade curiosity that also happens to be a genuine 4-seat (2+2) drop-top.
picks.whatToVerify: Age-related rubber degradation even at low miles: check all hoses, belts, and weatherstripping. Top motor and mechanism — 33-year-old hydraulics may need seals regardless of use. Inspect for any rodent damage in a car that may have sat. Fuel system for varnish. Get a pre-purchase inspection from someone familiar with older Japanese cars.
picks.bottomLine: A true low-mileage time capsule — wonderful if the mechanicals check out, a project if they don't.

picks.whyGood: The B8 A5 Cabriolet is an elegant 4-seat convertible with Audi's 2.0T TFSI and all-wheel drive. Good Deal rating. At $8,610 for a 2013 this is solid value; the Prestige trim means it came loaded.
picks.whatToVerify: 2.0T TFSI timing chain tensioner — check for any cold-start rattle (a known early-gen issue). Quattro haldex service history. Top power fabric condition and rear window clarity. Inspect for any DSG or S-tronic service needs. Pull a Carfax for any accident history.
picks.bottomLine: German drop-top luxury with AWD and a Good Deal rating — the refined choice in this batch.

picks.whyGood: A 2015 BMW 435i xDrive convertible — the most recent-generation F33 4-series — for $8,500 is eye-catching. 300hp N55 turbo inline-6 and all-wheel drive make it a capable all-season drop-top. Private seller pricing is often more negotiable.
picks.whatToVerify: N55 engine: check for any coolant leak at the expansion tank; electric water pump life (failure can cause overheating). Top hydraulics on the F33 — confirm full operation. xDrive transfer case and rear diff service history. At 140k miles ask specifically about timing chain and VANOS service.
picks.bottomLine: Newest platform in the Top 10 at the lowest asking price — high mileage is the trade-off for the modern 4-series.

mustangs.introHtml: Ford Mustang convertibles 2000+ within budget. Ranked by generation (newest first), then mileage.

picks.whyGood: The S550 EcoBoost Premium is the most refined Mustang convertible in this batch — modern safety tech, MagneRide option, modern infotainment. The 2.3L EcoBoost puts down 310hp and 350lb-ft. Fred Beans is an established PA dealer.
picks.whatToVerify: EcoBoost: check for any charge pipe or intercooler leaks; verify boost pressure is normal on a test drive. Convertible top motor full-cycle test. S550 rear suspension clunk check. Pull Carfax — 132k miles on a 2020 is high, so accident history and service records matter most.
picks.bottomLine: The most modern Mustang drop-top in the search — worth the mileage for the latest platform.

picks.whyGood: The last-gen S197 Mustang convertible at $9,900. Simple, well-supported V6 or GT, easy to service anywhere. Good price for the year and mileage.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm trim level and engine (V6 vs GT — price suggests V6). T-3650 gearbox 3rd-gear synchro test. Check rear-seat water staining from top seal. 8.8 rear axle clunk check on takeoff. Soft top condition — inspect rear window for crazing.
picks.bottomLine: S197 simplicity at a fair price — the most wrench-friendly Mustang convertible in the batch.

picks.whyGood: S550 generation at the top of budget — includes all the S550 improvements over S197 (independent rear suspension, better NVH). At a Lexus dealer, likely kept to a higher standard. 106k miles is manageable.
picks.whatToVerify: S550 rear subframe bushings. Electronic power steering feel — confirm normal assist. EcoBoost or V6? Confirm powertrain. Convertible top motor test. CarFax for prior owner count.
picks.bottomLine: Higher budget but gets you into the modern IRS S550 chassis — meaningful upgrade in comfort over the S197.

picks.whyGood: S197 last-gen refresh (2010+ restyled). Simple, proven V6 or V8 powertrain. At 117k miles the price feels high but S197 parts are abundant and cheap.
picks.whatToVerify: Convertible top motor and seals — check rear seats for any water intrusion. Frame rail rust at the convertible top mount bracket (S197 weak spot). Confirm V6 vs GT. 8.8 rear axle check. Soft top rear window condition.
picks.bottomLine: Slightly over-priced for the mileage, but a known quantity with great parts support.
